other_lo.note:
Rounding the LP is the one step of the fractional family that needs totality, and
$\mathrm{GapMaj}$ kills it. Any block that flips the answer at a promise input must move at
least $2\delta n$ coordinates, so a fractional block assignment obeys
$2\delta n \sum_B w_B \le \sum_i \sum_{B \ni i} w_B \le n$, i.e. $\mathrm{fbs}\le 1/(2\delta)$.
A $1$-certificate, on the other hand, must fix more than $n/2-\delta n$ ones: fix fewer and
setting every free coordinate to $0$ gives a completion that is still inside the promise and
is a $0$-input. For constant $\delta$ that is $O(1)$ against $\Omega(n)$.

Lower bounds / separations — there is a family achieving this

  • \(\mathrm{fbs}(\mathrm{GapMaj}^{\delta}_n) \le 1/(2\delta),\ \ \mathrm{C}(\mathrm{GapMaj}^{\delta}_n) > n/2-\delta n\)
    witness: \(\mathrm{GapMaj}^{\delta}_{n}\)
    Rounding the LP is the one step of the fractional family that needs totality, and $\mathrm{GapMaj}$ kills it. Any block that flips the answer at a promise input must move at least $2\delta n$ coordinates, so a fractional block assignment obeys $2\delta n \sum_B w_B \le \sum_i \sum_{B \ni i} w_B \le n$, i.e. $\mathrm{fbs}\le 1/(2\delta)$. A $1$-certificate, on the other hand, must fix more than $n/2-\delta n$ ones: fix fewer and setting every free coordinate to $0$ gives a completion that is still inside the promise and is a $0$-input. For constant $\delta$ that is $O(1)$ against $\Omega(n)$.

So $\mathrm{C}=O(\mathrm{fbs}^2)$, $\mathrm{C}=O(\mathrm{RC}^2)$ and the rest of the "round the fractional certificate" family are total-function theorems -- even though the reverse inequalities $\mathrm{fbs}\le\mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{fbs}=\Theta(\mathrm{RC})$ hold in every setting.

see also: \(\mathrm{C}(f)\), \(\mathrm{fbs}(f)\), \(\mathrm{RC}(f)\), \(\mathrm{GapMaj}^{\delta}_{n}\), Total functions, partial functions, and relations data/relations/08-fractional.yaml

facts: The maximum separation from bounded-error randomized queries is quadratic, with no log loss: $\mathrm{C}=\Omega(\mathrm{R}^2)$ on Ambainis–Iraids–Kokainis unambiguous DNF [AIK26]. Ben-David–Kothari championship function independently gives the same exponent with logarithmic slack [BenDavidKothari26].

The $\mathrm{C}/\mathrm{Q}$ and $\mathrm{C}/\widetilde{\deg}$ exponents are settled at $4$, up to logarithms [AIK26, BenDavidKothari26, Pabbaraju26]. Exact and zero-error quantum queries have a quadratic separation from $\mathrm{C}$, against a cubic universal upper bound [AIK26, KLLPV26].

\(At zero error the partition bound is at least certificate complexity, because zero error forces every subcube in the LP to be a genuine certificate.\) partial Settled #

Upper bounds — holds for every partial

  • \(\mathrm{C}(f) \le \mathrm{prt}_{0}(f)\)
    JainKlauck10
    [JainKlauck10, Thm 3.2]. At $\varepsilon = 0$ a subcube $A$ carrying weight under label $z$ must be a $z$-certificate: if some $x \in A$ had $f(x) \ne z$ then the correct weight at $x$ already sums to $1$, and adding $w_{A,z}>0$ would break completeness. So every subcube used at $x$ has $|A| \ge \mathrm{C}_x(f)$, and $\mathrm{prt}^{\mathrm{LP}}_0(f) \ge 2^{\mathrm{C}_x(f)}\sum_{A \ni x} w_{A,f(x)} = 2^{\mathrm{C}_x(f)}$. Note this is $\mathrm{C}$, not $\mathrm{D}$ -- the LP does not have to be consistent across inputs.

Deliberately kept out of the transitive closure. This bullet carries no form:, because the zoo indexes $\mathrm{prt}$ at its default error $\varepsilon = 1/3$ and the statement above holds only at $\varepsilon = 0$. Chaining the two would give $\mathrm{C}(f) \le \mathrm{prt}(f) \le 2\mathrm{R}(f)$, i.e. $\mathrm{C} = O(\mathrm{R})$, which is false -- $\mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{R}$ are quadratically separated. The honest bounded-error statement is the $\mathrm{RC} \to \mathrm{prt}$ record, and $\mathrm{C}$ is not below $\mathrm{prt}_{1/3}$.

see also: \(\mathrm{prt}_{\varepsilon}(f)\), \(\mathrm{C}(f)\), \(\mathrm{RC}(f)\), \(\mathrm{SP}(f)\) data/relations/11-lp-and-lower-bound-methods.yaml

  • \(\mathrm{C}(f) \le \overline{\mathrm{prt}}_{0}(f)\)·
    JainKlauck10 KLLRX15
    At $\varepsilon = 0$ the argument that every weighted subcube is a genuine certificate only needs $\sum_{A \ni x,z} w_{A,z} \le 1$ against $\sum_{A \ni x} w_{A,f(x)} \ge 1$, so it survives the relaxation. See the $\mathrm{RC} \to \overline{\mathrm{prt}}$ record.

As with $\mathrm{C} \to \mathrm{prt}$, this bullet carries no form: and is kept out of the closure: it is a zero-error statement, and the zoo indexes $\overline{\mathrm{prt}}$ at $\varepsilon = 1/3$.
